newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario economy poised for solid growth, bank says.
newsitem.headline: Ontario economy poised for solid growth, bank says.

text.p: Ontario's economy will grow briskly as strong consumer demand and a surge in exports lead to a substantial reduction in unemployment, said a forecast released on Thursday by one of Canada's largest banks.
The CIBC forecast that Ontario's economy would grow by about 3.6 percent in 1997 and by 3.1 percent in 1998.

"Almost every indicator points to an economy that has improved sharply over the first half of 1997," said Linda Nazareth, senior economist with CIBC. "With the exception of Alberta, this will be the strongest economic performance among the provinces."
Ontario's economy has rebounded from the recession of the early 1990s and is now benefitting from heavy demand for its goods in the United States.
Manufacturing shipments and retail sales have already jumped sharply in 1997, and the province created 118,000 jobs between February and June of this year.
The CIBC said exports, which were a major driver of Ontario's growth in the 1990s, would continue to rise but at a slightly slower pace.
A slowdown in the auto industry is likely to be offset by Ontario's growing high technology sector, the forecast suggested.
The CIBC also predicted employment in Ontario would grow by about 200,000 during the next two years, the strongest job creation since the late 1980s.
"This will take the province's unemployment rate well below 8.0 percent next year from the current level of 8.5 percent," Nazareth said.
Toronto is emerging as the fastest growing region of Ontario following a long period of sluggishness, with employment up 3.3 percent year over year.
The Toronto region will continue to outperform the rest of the province in 1998, the forecast concluded.
